about: Layout rules learned from real Nature figures, with the evidence for each. A rule enters only with a measurement behind it; a rule without evidence is a hypothesis and is marked as one.

rules.name: panel letters are figure-anchored, not axes-anchored
rules.rule: Place panel letters in FIGURE coordinates derived from the axes bounding box, offset by a fixed number of POINTS.
rules.why: Axes-relative placement (x=-0.30 in axes space) scales with panel width, so in a narrow panel the letter falls outside the canvas and is silently clipped. A figure was published this way with no visible 'a'.
rules.evidence: Measured: the demo figure rendered with panel 'a' absent at x=-0.30 axes coords, present at a -12 pt figure offset.

check.why: axes-relative panel letters get clipped in narrow panels

rules.name: column width is exact, not approximate
rules.rule: Width is exactly 89 or 183 mm. Never 'about 183'.
rules.why: A publisher rescales a figure that is off-width, which changes every type size in it. A 198.8 mm figure rescaled to 183 mm shrinks 5 pt text to 4.6 pt -- below the floor -- without anyone touching the figure.
rules.evidence: Measured: one committed figure at 198.8 mm; its 5 pt labels would land at 4.61 pt after rescale.

check.why: an unpinned bbox pads the output past the column width

rules.name: named text sizes are unsafe
rules.rule: Every text category must be an explicit number in points. Never 'large', 'small', 'medium'.
rules.why: matplotlib resolves 'large' to 1.2x the base size. With a 7 pt base that is 8.4 pt, above the 7 pt ceiling. The source reads 'large' and looks harmless; the PDF measures 8.4 pt.
rules.evidence: Measured: 8.4 pt on every panel title in two figures whose source said axes.titlesize='large'.

check.why: a named size such as 'large' resolves to 1.2x the base and lands above the ceiling

rules.name: log-axis exponents cannot meet the band
rules.rule: Replace 10^n labels with plain numbers on every log axis.
rules.why: matplotlib draws the exponent at ~0.7x the base size. Base 5.0 -> exponent 3.50 pt; 6.0 -> 4.20; 7.0 -> 4.90. The admissible band is 5-7 pt, so no base works. The fix is to stop using the notation.
rules.evidence: Measured exponents at 3.15-4.90 pt in rendered PDFs; the rcParams looked correct throughout.

check.why: 10^n exponents cannot meet the 5-7 pt band at any admissible base

rules.name: the save call can silently resize the figure
rules.why: Passing no bbox_inches to savefig is not enough: a style can set savefig.bbox='tight', which pads the output regardless. Three separate mechanisms moved the width before this was pinned.
rules.evidence: Measured: a figure created at exactly 183.00 mm was written to a 185.54 mm page.

check.why: the save call can silently resize the figure

rules.name: fonttype 3 looks correct and is rejected
rules.why: The community 'nature' style sets fonttype=3, which outlines text. Nature rejects outlined text. Nothing about the rendered figure looks wrong, so the defect survives every visual review.
rules.evidence: SciencePlots 'nature' style ships pdf.fonttype=3; measured in the applied rcParams.

check.why: Type-3 outlines are rejected by Nature

rules.name: source linting cannot catch these
rules.rule: Audit the rendered PDF, not the source.
rules.why: Every defect above was invisible in the source and visible in the output. A linter reading the code would have passed all six figures.
rules.evidence: Four of six figures carried sub-5 pt text while their generators read as correct.

check.why: source linting cannot catch these defects; the output must be audited

rules.name: panel-count ceiling
rules.rule: Prefer 3-4 panels per double-column figure; split rather than crowd.
rules.why: Observed in Nature figures and in the critique of this project's own fig1, which carried six panels of which three were tabular content.
rules.evidence: NOT MEASURED. This is a hypothesis from reading figures, not a measurement.
rules.unchecked_why: the report does not record panel counts, so the claimed 3-4 ceiling has nothing to be checked against; it is also a hypothesis with no measurement

rules.name: whitespace ratio
rules.rule: Content should occupy most of the canvas; large empty regions suggest a mis-sized panel.
rules.why: Plausible from the guide's 'minimizing white space', but no threshold has been measured.
rules.evidence: Measured on 6 of this pipeline's own figures: ink density 3.31-17.4% (mean 10.08%, spread 14.09 pp). The figures cluster, so the band is a rule.
rules.refuted_by: The first real Nature figure inspected (nwag582fig1) has an ink density of 35.8 %, far outside the 3.3-17.4 % band this rule claimed. The band was measured on six line-and-scatter plots from this project and generalised to 'figures', which it never supported.
rules.scope_where_it_did_hold: This project's own six figures, all of which are line/scatter plots. The band describes that genre, not figures in general.
rules.unchecked_why: REFUTED on 2026-10-18: the first real Nature figure inspected has 35.8% ink, far outside the 3.3-17.4% band this rule claimed. A refuted rule should not be checked; it should not be enforced

rules.name: published figures rarely sit at a stated column width
rules.rule: Observed published figure bands have a median width of 171.6 mm; only 27.6 % fall within 3 mm of 89 or 183 mm.
rules.why: If true, this separates the SPECIFICATION (a submission must be 89 or 183 mm) from OBSERVED PRACTICE (published figures are often scaled to other widths). Conflating the two was a core error in the earlier rules.
rules.evidence: Measured on 369 figure bands from 38 local Nature PDFs: p10 104.4, p25 139.8, median 171.6, p75 183.5, p90 200.0 mm; 16 near 89 mm, 86 near 183 mm.
rules.caveat: NOT YET TRUSTWORTHY. The figure-band detector is a heuristic that merges overlapping drawing/image rectangles; it may not recover true figure boundaries. LEARNINGS.md P0 requires a 20-band manual validation before this becomes verified.
rules.voided_because: Measured on the ink-rectangle-merging detector, which the adversarial audit showed was wrong for roughly half its output. The numbers are not merely imprecise, they are about a different population.
rules.correction_note: My earlier report said '52.1 % within a stated column width'. That used a +/-5 mm tolerance while this rule itself states +/-3 mm. At +/-3 mm the figure is 38.4 %. Reporting the wider tolerance doubled the apparent effect. Both are now recorded so the discrepancy is visible rather than replaced silently.
rules.unchecked_why: VOID: measured on the ink-rectangle-merging detector, which the adversarial audit showed was wrong for roughly half its output

rules.name: a third of published figure bands contain text below 5 pt
rules.rule: 34.0 % of measured figure bands contain at least one text span below 5 pt.
rules.why: The specification states a 5 pt minimum. If published figures routinely fall below it, then judging compliance by PDF RENDERED font size is a flawed metric -- the PDF may be generated larger and scaled down for print.
rules.evidence: Measured on 188 bands: min 3.0, p10 4.0, median 5.0, p90 7.0 pt; 34.0 % below 5 pt.
rules.caveat: Same detector caveat as E01, PLUS an unresolved scale question: PDF rendered size is not necessarily printed size. LEARNINGS.md P2.
rules.voided_because: Measured on the ink-rectangle-merging detector, which the adversarial audit showed was wrong for roughly half its output. The numbers are not merely imprecise, they are about a different population.
rules.unsupported_because: E02 is about FONT SIZE, and the caption-anchored records do not carry min_font_pt at all. The new detector does not measure type, so this rule has no measurement basis and cannot be re-derived until it does.
rules.unchecked_why: VOID: same broken detector, plus an unresolved scale question -- PDF rendered size is not necessarily printed size

rules.name: caption opens with a summary sentence
rules.rule: Observed in 189/196 (96.4 %) of the corpus captions.
rules.why: Does the caption's first sentence state what the whole figure shows, rather than starting a panel walk or a statistic?
rules.evidence: Measured from caption TEXT (not a vision model) over 196 captions from 34 Nature PDFs: 189/196 = 96.4 %. Main-text figures only: 118/124 = 95.2 %.
rules.caveat: This describes what published captions DO, not what a submission MUST do. It is not enforced and must not be treated as a requirement. The classifier is a text heuristic; its rules are pinned by tests and a mutation test proves the tests fail when the rule is broken.
rules.unchecked_why: describes CAPTION TEXT. figpipe draws figures and does not write captions, so no figure check can verify it

rules.name: captions walk the panels when there are panels
rules.rule: Observed in 65/196 (33.2 %) of the corpus captions.
rules.why: Does the caption address two or more panels explicitly ((a)/(b) or 'a, b,')?
rules.evidence: Measured from caption TEXT (not a vision model) over 196 captions from 34 Nature PDFs: 65/196 = 33.2 %. Main-text figures only: 48/124 = 38.7 %.
rules.caveat: This describes what published captions DO, not what a submission MUST do. It is not enforced and must not be treated as a requirement. The classifier is a text heuristic; its rules are pinned by tests and a mutation test proves the tests fail when the rule is broken.
rules.unchecked_why: describes CAPTION TEXT; out of scope for a figure pipeline

rules.name: captions state their statistics
rules.rule: Observed in 41/196 (20.9 %) of the corpus captions.
rules.why: Does the caption state n, a test, an interval, or an error definition?
rules.evidence: Measured from caption TEXT (not a vision model) over 196 captions from 34 Nature PDFs: 41/196 = 20.9 %. Main-text figures only: 23/124 = 18.6 %.
rules.caveat: This describes what published captions DO, not what a submission MUST do. It is not enforced and must not be treated as a requirement. The classifier is a text heuristic; its rules are pinned by tests and a mutation test proves the tests fail when the rule is broken.
rules.unchecked_why: describes CAPTION TEXT; out of scope for a figure pipeline

rules.name: captions usually do NOT put statistics last
rules.rule: Observed in 15/196 (7.6 %) of the corpus captions.
rules.why: Is the statistical material carried by the FINAL sentence?
rules.evidence: Measured from caption TEXT (not a vision model) over 196 captions from 34 Nature PDFs: 15/196 = 7.6 %. Main-text figures only: 8/124 = 6.5 %.
rules.caveat: This describes what published captions DO, not what a submission MUST do. It is not enforced and must not be treated as a requirement. The classifier is a text heuristic; its rules are pinned by tests and a mutation test proves the tests fail when the rule is broken.
rules.unchecked_why: describes CAPTION TEXT; out of scope for a figure pipeline

rules.name: a plate is not a swatch
rules.rule: A figure with more than one panel is built by figpipe.composite: every panel carries exactly one 8 pt letter, and one gutter width runs through the whole plate.
rules.why: Six single-panel templates produced one axes each, so the library could draw a swatch but not the plate a paper actually prints. The composer owns the geometry; the panel only owns its drawing. An empty grid cell, an uneven gutter and a missing letter are all visible defects, and a composer without a read-back check ships them silently.
rules.evidence: Measured on the caption-anchored corpus (73 real figures): 36 composites, of which 29 had every internal boundary inside an empty band; gutter median None mm (n=61), panel aspect median 1.34 (n=90), and every one of 46 detected panel letters was 8.0 pt.

check.why: composes a real four-panel plate and reads the letters, gutters and page size back; a composer that stack panels on top of each other fails it

schema_note: v2 splits the old single `verified` flag into `mechanism_verified` (code enforces it AND a test locks it) and `empirically_measured` (a measurement supports it). `enforced` requires both. The old flag conflated these and let a rule be marked verified while nothing enforced it.

check_coverage.note: Derived from the rules on every run, not stored by a migration. A rule with check=None is reported UNCHECKED and never counted as passing.

distinction.specification: What a SUBMISSION must satisfy. Stated by the journal. figpipe enforces these: exact 89/183 mm, 5-7 pt type, vector, fonttype 42.
distinction.observed_practice: What PUBLISHED figures do. Measured from the corpus. May differ from the specification because of scaling at typesetting, genre differences, or the specification describing intent rather than outcome.
distinction.why_it_matters: The earlier rules used 'verified' for both, which let a genre-specific observation (H02) masquerade as a general rule. L-rules are specification; E-rules are observed practice; they are not interchangeable.

corpus.source: local Nature PDF corpus (D:\2026-AI4S), filenames containing NATURE
corpus.superseded_because: The 369-band figures came from the ink-rectangle detector the audit found ~50 % wrong. Current corpus is corpus/figures_caption_anchored.json (73 figures, 11 papers, caption-anchored).

caption_study.method: measured from the caption string; no VLM involved, because the local model was shown to fabricate figure properties (20 assertions across 3 control images, verdict FABRICATES)

composite_study.method: Each figure's caption-anchored bbox is rendered at 300 dpi and binarised (ink = grey < 200). Panel letters are read from the PDF's own text spans (single characters a-h, 7-9.5 pt). Full captions come from corpus/caption_features.jsonl joined through the extraction manifests; the caption letter counter accepts only forms Nature writes: '(a)', 'a,', 'a;', 'a-c' ranges, 'Figure 1a'. The panel count is the detected letter count, falling back to the caption count, falling back to 1. For a count of n the factor pairs (rows, cols) are enumerated; a boundary starts at the next letter's position (letters sit at the panel's top-left, so the split is just left of the following letter) or at equal division, and is refined to the emptiest 0.8 mm band within +-15 mm on the ink projection. A grid is accepted when every cell holds ink and has aspect in 0.15-8. Gutters are the ink-free run around the accepted boundary, in mm.
